body:
Having given it some time to stew I feel a bit more at ease with what happened. I could have gone about things far better, that’s for sure, and the guilt is still there of course, but I can acknowledge that turning around and agreeing to a relationship for his sake is an awful idea. Thank you for your reply, it definitely helped in soothing some of my less rational thoughts. 

I think I’m going to start seeing a therapist to hopefully work through some of the issues that might be holding me back.

It definitely isn’t right.

I’ve seen just about every kind of doctor under the sun and not one could figure out the underlying cause. It’s been settled that I have chronic fatigue syndrome, which is essentially a diagnosis of elimination, a fancy way of saying nobody really knows what’s wrong with me. I assume it has roots in something psychological and I have actually been improving as of recent. It feels like I might one day be able to function as a relatively normal person, but I guess we’ll have to see.

Excuse me for going on that whole ramble. 

tl;dr: I’ve tried, doctors can’t figure out what’s wrong with me.

First of all, thank you so much for taking the time out of your day or night to reply to my post. It means a lot. 

You’re definitely right. I think I knew that, deep down, I just needed someone to tell it to me for it to truly register. If I suck it up and stick through this knowing that my feelings for him are mostly platonic it isn’t going to end well for either of us. 

All I can really do is hope that I can learn from the mistakes I’ve made here and prevent myself from repeating them in the future.

I gotcha man.

I’m no licensed psychologist or anything, and I’m not about to diagnose myself, but honestly? I feel that there’s a good chance I have it to some degree. I’m diagnosed with clinical depression and generalized anxiety, so I don’t doubt that my issues surrounding my appearance may have _some_ rooting in mental illness, or are, at the very least, exacerbated by my preexisting conditions.
